title: Localization at closed-fibre regular scalars is universally injective
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of commutative local rings, with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_R,\mathfrak m_S$, meaning that the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_S$ is $\mathfrak m_R$. Assume that $S=W^{-1}B$ as an $R$-algebra, where $B$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and $W$ is a multiplicative subset [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Let $N$ be a finitely presented $S$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] which is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Put $\overline N=N/\mathfrak m_RN$ and $\Sigma=\{s\in S:\overline N\xrightarrow{z\mapsto sz}\overline N\text{ is injective}\}$. This set contains $1$ and is closed under multiplication. For each $s\in\Sigma$, multiplication $N\xrightarrow{s}N$ is universally injective over $R$: for every $R$-module $L$, multiplication by $s$ on $N\otimes_R L$ is injective. Moreover the localization map $N\to\Sigma^{-1}N$, $n\mapsto n/1$, is universally injective over $R$: for every $R$-module $L$ the induced map $N\otimes_R L\to(\Sigma^{-1}N)\otimes_R L$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 05DF (lemma-homothety-universally-injective), with its inherited assumptions from lemma-homothety-spectrum; the Noetherian finite closed-fibre assumptions follow from the displayed finite presentations.

proof.text: Multiplication by $1$ on $\overline N$ is the identity. If $s,t\in\Sigma$ and $stz=0$, injectivity of multiplication by $s$ gives $tz=0$, and that of multiplication by $t$ gives $z=0$. Hence $1\in\Sigma$ and $st\in\Sigma$.

source.place: Tag 05DF, notation inherited from Tag 05DE: multiplicative set of closed-fibre regular elements

proof.text: Fix $s\in\Sigma$. Apply the general local closed-fibre injectivity criterion to $u:N\to N$, $n\mapsto sn$. This is $S$-linear since $S$ is commutative. The local map and presentation $S=W^{-1}B$ supply its local essentially finitely presented algebra; both modules are the given finitely presented $N$, its target is $R$-flat, and its reduction is injective by the definition of $\Sigma$. Thus $u$ is injective and $Q=N/sN$ is $R$-flat. The quotient map gives $0\to N\xrightarrow{s}N\to Q\to0$.

source.place: Tag 05DF, first proof sentence; Algebra Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general)

proof.text: Let $L$ be any $R$-module. Apply tensor injectivity for a short exact sequence with flat quotient to the sequence of Step 2. It gives injectivity of $1_L\otimes u$ on $L\otimes_RN$. The tensor universal property defines mutually inverse flips $n\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes n$ and $x\otimes n\mapsto n\otimes x$. On a pure tensor, flipping, applying $1_L\otimes u$, and flipping back sends $n\otimes x$ to $sn\otimes x$. Pure tensors generate, so this composite is multiplication by $s$ on $N\otimes_RL$. It is injective. This proves the first universal-injectivity assertion for every $s\in\Sigma$.

source.place: Tag 05DF, second proof sentence; Algebra Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero); tensor symmetry expanded from its universal property

proof.text: Keep $L$ arbitrary and put $X=N\otimes_RL$, with its $S$-action through $N$. Apply localization commuting with tensor over the base, with $A=S$, $T=\Sigma$ and $M=N$. Step 1 supplies the multiplicative subset. This identifies $\Sigma^{-1}X$ with $(\Sigma^{-1}N)\otimes_RL$ by $(n\otimes x)/s\mapsto(n/s)\otimes x$, and identifies the tensor of $N\to\Sigma^{-1}N$ with $z\mapsto z/1$.

source.place: Tag 05DF, final proof sentence, localization step expanded using Algebra Tags 00DK/00D2

proof.text: If $z\in X$ maps to zero under the map of Step 4, then $z/1=0$ in $\Sigma^{-1}X$. The fraction-zero criterion gives $s\in\Sigma$ with $sz=0$. Step 3 says multiplication by this $s$ on $X$ is injective, so $z=0$. The map is therefore injective for every $L$, proving the localization assertion.
